This in turn implies the stronger condition of vanishing for k + i ≥ p. The
definition for a finitely generated graded R -module M , which extends that
for sheaves was given by Eisenbud and Goto [EG84], and regularity was
investigated later by several people, notably Bayer and Mumford [BM93],
Bayer and Stillman [BS87], Eisenbud and Goto [EG84], and Ooishi [Ooi82].

generated graded R -module, then the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of M ,
denoted by reg(M ), is an invariant that measures the “size” of its minimal
free resolution and the complexity of the given module. Recall that a graded
